info.name: ImageFX
info.comment: Renders a bitmap image in the effect pipeline.

description.p: The ImageFX class will render a source image into a given rectangle within the current user coordinate system. The client has the option of providing a pre-allocated Bitmap or the path to a Image file as the source.

If a pre-allocated Bitmap is to be used, it must be owned by the ImageFX object before the ImageFX is initialised. The bitmap can be created as a child of the uninitialised ImageFX, or an existing bitmap can be assigned to it with SetOwner. The bitmap must be initialised before the ImageFX. The default IMAGE mode requires 32 bits per pixel with an alpha channel. The bitmap is retained for the lifetime of the ImageFX. An attempt to free it earlier is deferred until the ImageFX is freed. Changes to the content of the bitmap are rendered on the next draw of the filter. Call Vector.Refresh() on the filtered vector to ensure that it is redrawn.
If a source image file is referenced, it will be upscaled to meet the requirements automatically as needed.

Setting OutputMode to HEIGHT produces a floating-point map for effects such as TileFX and LightingFX. A BMF::GREYSCALE bitmap supplies its full 16-bit samples, including when loaded from a 16-bit greyscale PNG. For other formats, HeightChannel selects the stored channel to read, with red as the default. Heights are normalised to the range 0 to 1 and resampled without colour-space conversion.

Technically the ImageFX object is represented by a new viewport, the bounds of which are defined by attributes X, Y, Width and Height. The placement and scaling of the referenced image is controlled by the AspectRatio field.

action.name: Draw
action.comment: Render the effect to the target bitmap.
action.prototype: ERR acDraw(*Object, DOUBLE X, DOUBLE Y, DOUBLE Width, DOUBLE Height)

input.param: The X position of the region to be drawn.
The Y position of the region to be drawn.
The width of the region to be drawn.
The height of the region to be drawn.

field.name: Bitmap
field.comment: The Bitmap being used as the image source.

description.p: Reading the Bitmap field will return the Bitmap that is being used as the image source. A custom Bitmap is assigned by making the ImageFX object its owner prior to initialisation, as described in the class overview.
If an image has been processed by setting the Path, the Bitmap will refer to the content that has been processed.

field.name: HeightChannel
field.comment: Selects the stored channel to read in height mode.

description.p: A 16-bit greyscale bitmap supplies its grey samples regardless of this setting. For other bitmaps, alpha reads as 1 when the bitmap has no alpha channel.

field.name: OutputMode
field.comment: Selects image or floating-point height output.

field.name: Path
field.comment: Path to an image file supported by the Image class.

field.name: ResampleMethod
field.comment: The resample algorithm to use for transforming the source image.

field.name: XMLDef
field.comment: Returns an SVG compliant XML string that describes the filter.

constants.comment: Aspect ratios control alignment, scaling and clipping.
constants.const: Aspect ratio is preserved. The entire viewbox will be visible in the viewport. The viewbox is scaled up as much as possible.
Scale the viewbox to match the size of the viewport. Aspect ratio is not preserved.
Aspect ratio is preserved. The viewbox can extend beyond the viewport's edges on one axis. The viewbox is scaled up as much as possible.
Align to the right.
Align to the horizontal center.
Align to the left.
Align to the bottom.
Align to the vertical center.
Align to the top.

constants.comment: Output modes for ImageFX, TurbulenceFX and BlurFX.
constants.const: Produce a linear floating-point height between 0 and 1 for enhanced lighting or height-mode blur.
Produce the usual RGBA image. This is the default.

constants.comment: Channel selection for scalar maps, such as height, ambient occlusion and roughness maps.
constants.const: The alpha channel.
The blue channel.
The green channel, which is the roughness channel of a packed ORM map.
The luminance of the stored red, green and blue values, weighted 0.2126, 0.7152 and 0.0722.
The red channel. This is the default, and the occlusion channel of a packed ORM map.
The default option is chosen by the system. This will typically be BILINEAR, but slow machines may switch to nearest neighbour and high speed machines could use more advanced methods.
Uses a broad Bessel filter that can preserve detail during resampling, but is slower than the smaller-kernel methods.
Produces a similar result to BILINEAR at a slightly higher CPU cost and a marginally sharper after-effect.
Bilinear is a common algorithm that produces a reasonable quality image quickly.
Five times slower than BILINEAR, the final result will be less sharp than SINC.
Uses a Gaussian filter that softens the result, reducing aliasing at the cost of sharp edge detail.
Uses a Kaiser-windowed filter, giving smooth interpolation with low ringing and a cost close to BILINEAR.
This well known algorithm may serve as a point of comparison for evaluating the results of other methods. It shares characteristics with SINC and BLACKMAN.
Uses a Mitchell-Netravali filter, balancing sharpness and smoothness at a cost similar to BICUBIC.
Nearest neighbour is the fastest sampler at the cost of poor quality.
Uses a quadratic filter with a modest kernel, giving smoother results than BILINEAR with limited extra cost.
Five times slower than BILINEAR, the final result is of very good quality.

About twice as slow as BILINEAR, this method samples a 4x4 area and produces a considerably better result, and is a good choice for enlarging images without producing artifacts when contrasting colours are present.
